newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar may extend range slightly upwards in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar may extend range slightly upwards in Asia.

text.p: The dollar's moves in Asian trade on Tuesday are likely to be a close twin of those in New York's session overnight, although its range is expected to be extended slightly upwards, dealers said.

But the dollar's overall moves against the yen are expected to be limited, with Japanese operators adopting a wait-and-see stance ahead of the release of the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey, the "tankan", due on Wednesday.
Buying of dollars against European currencies, especially the mark and possibly the Swiss franc and sterling as well, is likely to provide energy for the greenback's moves on the yen.
"The overall moves appear to be inspired more by a stronger dollar than a weaker yen," one trust bank dealer said.

The yen was initially sold on Monday after Bank of Japan (BOJ) executive director Tadayo Honma said continued failures of Japanese financial institutions could not be ruled out, suggesting that Japan's historically low official discount rate, now at 0.5 percent, was likely to remain unchanged.

While dealers said this comment had already been digested by the market, they warned that the emergence of similar comments today, or rumours about the tankan, could cause volatile dollar moves in the market's current nervous state.
Rubin told Reuters on Monday that the Clinton administration has no plans to change its strong-dollar policy despite increasing criticism from U.S. manufacturing companies.
"A strong dollar helps to keep interest rates down, helps to keep inflation down... It's very much in our interest," he said.
He added that he did not know whether Japan was manipulating the currency market to keep the yen down.
His comments slightly relieved market concerns about the U.S. stance, but otherwise had no impact, the city bank dealer said.
